brain.event_threshold: The confidence of the model's Should it do something soon? answer below which the decision is wait. Higher is a more patient lodger. Live. Default: 0.4.
brain.force_rules: Uses the rule brain even with a model loaded. For comparing the two from the log, whose brain= says which decided. Default: false.
brain.most_plans: How many plans it holds at once; it asks again every plan_every while below it (calm 2, intense 4, relentless 5; one before, owner: "one event at a time kinda gets slow"). Default: 3.
brain.plan_every: Seconds of the target's play between planning asks, on top of the trigger asks; 15 at least. Default: 90.
brain.queue: Checked (1 at least) but not read: the queue holds 64 questions whatever this says (MAX_QUEUED in model/queue.rs). A full queue refuses; the rule brain answers. Default: 64.
brain.react_threshold: The same for the model's Should it answer this? after a trigger (live): below it, no answer. Reactions are cheaper to get wrong than plans, so the bar is higher. Default: 0.55.
brain.temperature: How the answer is picked from the model's scores. 0: always the best choice, so the same situation gets the same answer every time, as the engine did. Above 0: a seeded draw weighted by the scores, sharper near 0, the model's own odds at 1, flatter above. The draws start from a seed that differs per start, joined by the world's seed. See Picking. Default: 0.7.
brain.text: How signs, chat lines and names get their words. generate (the default, the owner's call): the model writes the line itself, shown the bank for that kind of line as examples, a few words at most, letters and spaces only, through a blocklist, every line logged, and the bank used when a check fails. bank: the model picks among eight of the bank's lines for that kind, as it picks a choice (brain/text.rs). See Text. Default: "generate".
brain.text_temperature: How freely the model writes a sign or a line: 0 is the likeliest word every time (the same moment, the same line), higher draws among the likely ones (top 90 per cent). Lowered after lines repeated. Default: 0.8.
enabled: Whether a lodger moves into new worlds and existing ones keep theirs. false ends the stay in every world, where /craftkit lodger leave ends one gently. Default: true.
events.chat: Whether the lodger may touch the target's chat and player list (a line in their own name, a whisper from themselves, their name twice in the list, the joined and left lines, the sleepers count). Default: true.
events.cooldown_scale: Multiplies every event's cooldown. 2.0 is a lodger that repeats itself half as often and so does less. Default: 1.0.
events.disabled: Event ids the brain never offers as choices. For servers that want, say, no take or no sign_word. See Events. Default: [].
events.figure: Whether the far presence and the replay figure are ever shown. Default: true.
events.glitches: Whether the client-rendered glitches (the flicker, the lights failing, the sun blinking, the red rain, the fog, the crosshair gone, the camera nudge, the field of view pulled, the music cut, the silence) may happen. Default: true.
events.min_distance: Blocks from the target within which nothing that changes a block happens while it is in view (calm 80, intense 48, relentless 32; 24 before, when the owner watched torches go up from farther off). Lowering it is the one way to make the lodger bolder, and it is still bounded by the rules. Default: 64.
events.offered: How many eligible events the brain is offered per plan. Fewer is a more predictable lodger; more is a longer prompt. Default: 8.
events.sounds: Whether the sounds (the door and chest sounds, the knocks, the late steps, the mining sounds, the pet's growl) may happen. Off, nothing in the group is offered or forced. Default: true.
events.temper: Whether how they treat it moves its temper (chasing the figure, breaking its lights or house, lighting or flooding its place, cursing it in chat up; building or leaving a chest at its place, watching the figure from afar, kind words down; a tenth of the way back each day), and its temper the pace: the day's events half again at the top and half at the bottom, a stage's least days halved above 0.7 and most stretched by half below 0.2, the bolder events a stage early above 0.6 and late below 0.2, three quarters of events.min_distance above 0.8, a fiercer fight, and the ending. It rests at 0.2 on calm, 0.3 on balanced, 0.4 on intense, 0.5 on relentless. false keeps it at rest. See Provocation and temper. Default: true.
log.decisions: Writes every decision to config/lodger/decisions.log. Keep it on while developing; see The decision log. Default: true.
log.keep_mb: The log rotates past this size, keeping one older file. Default: 16.
model.context: The context window, in tokens; llama.cpp wants a multiple of 32. The situation text plus one question and its longest choice must fit: the memory's detail lines (habits, places, people) are taken only while they fit, at 3.5 characters a token with 200 tokens kept for the frame and the question (memory::describe_chars). Larger costs memory (about 30 KB a token for the 1.5B), not speed. It was 512 (owner: "can we increase context window ... to 1500?"). Default: 1536.
model.enabled: Whether the model is used at all. false downloads nothing, and the simpler built-in rules decide what it does; a player who only joins servers (where the server's model decides) needs nothing more. The download screen's Play without it sets it, and the settings' Use the model turns it back on, which brings the download screen up. Default: true.
model.gpu_share: The share of the model's layers run on the GPU (Vulkan on Windows and Linux, Metal on a Mac), the rest on the CPU: 0 the CPU alone, 1 all of it, the default (owner: "by default the full model should run on the gpu"; it was half before, after "limit it to like 50% gpu cuz it makes my game stutter"). With no GPU, all of it runs on the CPU whatever this says. The prompt is decoded in chunks of 64 tokens with a rest between (model.pause_ms), so no frame waits on one long burst; if the game still stutters, lower this. The old model.gpu_layers it replaced was never passed on, and llama.cpp put every layer on the GPU. Default: 1.
model.idle_minutes: Unloads the model after this long with no target online. Loading again takes a second or two. Default: 10.
model.path: Where the model is kept. Empty means config/lodger/models/<the size's file name>. Relative to the game directory unless absolute. Must be a loose file: llama.cpp maps it. Default: empty.
model.pause_ms: Milliseconds the model rests between each piece of its work while it thinks (every 64 tokens of a question, and before each piece when above 1): higher leaves more of the GPU and the CPU to the game at any moment, and its answers come slower; the game never waits on them either way. 0 to 100; the settings page steps it by 5. Owner: "is there a way to limit the amount of compute it uses". Default: 1.
model.size: Which model to run: 1.5b (1.1 GB, about 1.6 GB of RAM, a few hundred milliseconds a question; the default, the owner's call, for sharper judgment and better words), 0.5b (491 MB, about 700 MB of RAM, tens of milliseconds) , 3b (2.1 GB, about 2.6 GB of memory, slower again; Qwen's research license) or 4b, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (2.5 GB, about 3.2 GB of memory, the best reader). Changing it downloads the new file at the next start; the old one stays until deleted. See Which model. Default: "1.5b".
model.threads: Threads llama.cpp uses while scoring. More is faster and takes more from the game. Default: 2.
model.url: Where to fetch from. Empty means Qwen's own q4_k_m file for model.size on Hugging Face. Default: empty.
multiplayer.pick: Who the lodger moves in with when several players are on: model asks the brain once two are seen (Which player does it move in with?, their ordinals as the choices; live), first takes the first player seen. Alone for five minutes, the first seen is it either way. Default: "model".
multiplayer.retarget: Whether the lodger may change target once, at a stage's beginning from stage two, if the current one has not been seen for multiplayer.absent_days real days (by the computer's clock) and someone else is here. It keeps its want, its place, its house and what it did, and lets the old target's home, chests, habits and favourites go. Default: true.
multiplayer.witness_traces: Whether witnesses see traces at all. false holds back every change to the world (the house, their things, a sign) within 48 blocks of another player until they are gone, so only the target sees its work: a different and lonelier mod. Sounds, figures, the screen and chat go to the target alone either way. Default: true.
preset: calm, balanced, intense or relentless: a set of values for the keys below (see Presets). A key the file names wins over the preset; the file written back shows the preset's values filled in. Picking another preset on the settings screen takes the old preset's values out of the file, the ones you never changed, so the new preset's apply, and writes the file again with them. Default: "balanced".
stages.ending: "difficulty", "leave", "take" or "keep". Which ending the last stage works toward; "difficulty" reads the world's. See How it ends. Default: "difficulty".
stages.events_per_day: The budget of events per in-game day in each stage. Sounds count half. Stage five has its ending's script besides (its budget was 0 before, and its own rows, arrow_hits among them, could never run). See How often. Default: [1, 2, 4, 6, 3].
stages.least_days: The least in-game days each stage lasts, in order. See The five stages. Default: [1, 2, 2, 3, 1].
stages.most_days: The most. A stage that has not ended on its own ends here. Default: [3, 5, 5, 7, 3].
stages.start_after_days: In-game days a world is played before the lodger moves in. A fresh world is a fresh world first. Default: 3.
